title: Aim at the flag, or aim upstream? Aim upstream: 83 s. Aim at the flag: 139 s, nearly twice as long
description:
Aim at the flag, or aim upstream? The same river twice, seen from above: 50 m wide with a uniform current of 0.8 m/s everywhere (the same at the banks and in the middle), flowing down the screen. Two swimmers who both move at 1.0 m/s relative to the water (the current is 0.8 of their swimming speed, eight tenths) start on the near bank directly across from a flag on the far bank, at the same instant. Top panel: the swimmer who always points straight at the flag, velocity 1.0 m/s toward the flag plus the current. Bottom panel: the swimmer who holds one fixed heading, asin(0.8 / 1.0) = 53.13 degrees upstream of straight across, so the upstream part of the swimming speed, 0.8 m/s, cancels the current and the track is a straight line across at sqrt(v^2 - u^2) = 0.6 m/s. Both are integrated by classical RK4 at 0.001 s steps with a half-step rerun as a check; the flag swimmer is stopped within 1 mm of the flag by bisection inside the step, and the last millimetre is covered at the closing speed v - u = 0.2 m/s. Closed forms: w / sqrt(v^2 - u^2) for the upstream swimmer; w v / (v^2 - u^2) for the flag swimmer, whose track is the pursuit curve r = w cos^(k-1)(phi) / (1 + sin phi)^k with k = v / u = 1.25 (r the distance to the flag, phi the heading upstream of straight across). Shown at 5x speed, one run in 40 s. Deterministic, no seed.

Measured:
- aim upstream: heading 53.130 degrees, across at 0.6000 m/s; lands at 83.333333 s (closed form 83.3333 s, diff 1.2e-10 s); the track stays 0.0 m from the straight line; the half-step rerun moves the landing by 3.2e-10 s
- aim at the flag: within 1 mm of the flag at 138.883889 s and at the flag at 138.888889 s (closed form 138.888889 s, diff 3.4e-13 s); 1.6667 times the upstream swimmer's time, 55.56 s longer; the half-step rerun moves the landing by 1.4e-12 s
- the flag swimmer is swept 16.8852 m downstream first, furthest at 42.7368 s, 37.3361 m across, heading 53.130 degrees upstream there, the same angle the upstream swimmer holds (closed form 16.8852 m, the time by quadrature 42.7368 s)
- the RK4 track stays within 1.9e-12 m of the pursuit curve while more than 10 m from the flag and within 2.2e-09 m while more than 1 m from it
- when the upstream swimmer lands at 83.33 s the flag swimmer is 49.13 m across, 11.09 m downstream, 11.13 m from the flag, heading 85.5 degrees upstream, with 55.56 s still to swim at a net speed of 0.2118 m/s
- the flag swimmer's heading: 30 degrees at 25.89 s, 45 at 36.70 s, 60 at 48.24 s, 75 at 63.45 s, 85 at 81.74 s, 89 at 100.68 s; it reaches 49.9 m across at 102.82 s and crawls the rest up the far bank
- the flag swimmer's track: 20.0 s: 19.55 m across, 12.4 m downstream; 40.0 s: 35.63 across, 16.8 down; 60.0 s: 45.06 across, 15.3 down; 80.0 s: 48.84 across, 11.7 down; 100.0 s: 49.85 across, 7.8 down; 120.0 s: 50.00 across, 3.8 down
- current 0.5 m/s: aim upstream 30.0 degrees, lands at 57.74 s; aim at the flag lands at 66.67 s, 1.15 times longer, swept 9.62 m downstream
- current 0.9 m/s: aim upstream 64.2 degrees, lands at 114.71 s; aim at the flag lands at 263.16 s, 2.29 times longer, swept 20.11 m downstream
- current 1 m/s, equal to the swim speed: aim upstream needs 90 degrees, straight into the current, swimming in place, it never crosses; aim at the flag never lands: after 1200 s it is 50.0000 m across and 25.0000 m downstream, 25.0000 m from the flag, moving at 3.6e-12 m/s; the limit point is (50, 25) m, half the width downstream, reached within 1 mm from 283.0 s
- the drifter who points straight across and lets the current take it: lands 40.0 m downstream after 50.0 s
- checks: RK4 at 0.001 s against the closed forms (diffs 1.2e-10 and 3.4e-13 s), the half-step rerun (3.2e-10 and 1.4e-12 s), the straight line held to 0.0 m, the furthest point against the closed form (diffs 9.1e-10 m and 2.9e-09 s)

Why: the swimmer who always points at the flag starts out pointed almost straight across, so the current carries it downstream; the further it is swept, the more it must turn into the current, until near the far bank it is pointing straight upstream and gaining on the flag at only 1.0 minus 0.8 = 0.2 m/s. The swimmer who aims upstream from the start spends 0.8 m/s of swimming speed cancelling the current the whole way and keeps 0.6 m/s for the crossing: a straight line, 50 m at 0.6 m/s is 83.3 s. The pursuit takes w v / (v^2 - u^2), the straight line w / sqrt(v^2 - u^2), so the ratio is v / sqrt(v^2 - u^2): 1.6667 at this current, and it grows without bound as the current approaches the swimming speed.
